violation_type.title: Adequate Lighting During Naptime (26 TAC §746.2911)
violation_type.typical_finding: In the 3 to 5 yr old classroom the room had inadequte light and the children were not visable. The caregiver could not see the children.

finding_variants.text: In the 3 to 5 yr old classroom the room had inadequte light and the children were not visable. The caregiver could not see the children.
During a walk through of the center, a classroom did not have enough lighting in the room during nap time. This was corrected at inspection.
During the inspection I observed that the lighting in the nap area was too dark. Due to the lack of lighting, it was difficult to navigate the classroom. This is a violation of minimum standards.

The lighting in the infant room was low enough that the caregiver was not seen sitting on the floor during nap time.    Note: this was corrected at inspection when the director turned on the hallway light that adequately illuminated the infant room through the hallway windows.
The lighting in the four year old classroom was completely dark to the point where the light had to be turned on to adequately see the children in the room.
The Toddler room was too dark to count the children during naptime.    NOTE: The deficiency was corrected with additional lighting turned on from a closet space.
